title: Dashboard
description: Renders a grid of registered dashboard widgets. Reads manifest `dashboardWidget` blocks + admin.json `dashboardWidgets` overrides and mounts each widget as a tile.

documentation.purpose: Host app for the dashboard widget grid. Bundles the widget composition + tile rendering for any region using the `core:dashboard-grid` template (or any region — the host's grid container is part of its own DOM tree). Each tile mounts the widget app via the shared `MountedApp` resolver so the existing 4-layer cap gating + theming applies uniformly.

reads.purpose: Per-widget overrides (position / size / hidden) keyed by app id.
Read each app's `dashboardWidget` manifest block — only apps declaring one are eligible widgets.

states.renders: Grid of tiles, one per surviving widget.

states.when: composeWidgets() returns an empty list (no eligible widgets or all hidden)

a11y.focus-management: Tab order follows widget registration order. Each tile is a `region` landmark via the kernel; the host renders tiles as plain `<div>` since the kernel's region wrapper already supplies landmark roles for widgets that need them.

constraints.note: An app participates iff its manifest declares a `dashboardWidget` block. Programmatic registrations via `wp_admin_shell_register_dashboard_widget()` flow through the manifest registry — the registry adds a synthetic `dashboardWidget` block onto the host's app manifest, so the same gating applies.

The host is config-driven only — widgets are computed from `composeWidgets(manifests, overrides)` once per (manifests, overrides) tuple. Adding a widget at runtime requires the PHP side to update the manifest registry + cascade output, which happens at page load. Drag-to-reorder is out of scope for v1.

design-system-leakage.purpose: The host is DS-light — it renders structural `<div>` chrome only. Widget tiles inherit WPDS via the active engine's chrome bindings.
